items.title: George Mitchell Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: So that's the way I got started with Jelly. And, uh, he called me and, uh, uh, I'd come down to rehearsal and make some recordings.

ctx.x: Joe's, Joe's ideas, that's what I mean. If Joe had, uh, had, could handle his instrument, like Lewis, well, I, liked his ideas of the things that he would do. He played. He could play some of, some of the pretty ton of melodies in the thing. Well, Lewis, Lewis can do. Yeah, he plays a nice second part too. Yeah, yeah, yeah, Lewis. But, uh, I, I, I, I like, like, uh, Joe's ideas. He had a lot of good ideas on it. But, he, he, he couldn't, he wasn't, couldn't handle his trumpet as well as, as well as.

I wanted to ask you about those Jelly Roll Martin recordings. So many people, including me, think they're about the greatest records that we ever heard, the greatest ever made. If you could tell us about when you first met Jelly Roll, and how you started to play with him, and made some of those records.

Oh, well, uh, with Jelly, I don't know how I got started with Jelly. Let's see. It, uh, you see, I was working on a study job, around here at that time. And Jelly, he was recording. And, uh, I think, uh, one time there, something happened that he couldn't, the fellas that he had, uh, planned on using, why they, I don't know where, what happened. But, he, uh, they, they didn't work out. And, so you know how you have to do and you have to scout around and get someone. So that's the way I got started with Jelly.…
